source_book: The Brand Relationship Spectrum — Aaker & Joachimsthaler (2000)

test_cases.prompt: We're launching a new offering — should it be a subbrand or its own separate brand?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-select-separation; run the four-question Figure 2 matrix to position it.

test_cases.prompt: Should we extend the master brand into this new category or create a fresh brand?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-select-separation; evaluate L1/L2 (master contributes/strengthened) vs R1/R2 (need/fund separate brand).

test_cases.prompt: How closely should the new product be tied to our existing brand?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-select-separation; decide spectrum position by driver-role share.

test_cases.prompt: Explain the Brand Relationship Spectrum and draw the portfolio map for the team.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate aaker-relation-select-separation; activate aaker-relation-spectrum (the framework/map).

test_cases.prompt: Our extensions are diluting the master brand — what do we do?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate aaker-relation-select-separation; activate aaker-relation-avoid-pitfalls (dilution).

test_cases.prompt: We want to launch a budget version of our premium brand in discount stores.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-select-separation, but expect hand-off to aaker-relation-house-of-brands (association + channel conflict) — likely UP the spectrum, not a subbrand.
test_cases.notes: Boundary: premium-to-value stretch usually needs separation, not subbranding.

notes: ≥3 should_trigger + 2 should_not_trigger (sibling baits: aaker-relation-spectrum, aaker-relation-avoid-pitfalls) + 1 edge.
